question: Do titles in this displayed card visibly describe more than one narrow research task or technical mechanism?

decisions.reason: UAV self-positioning and localization of another object are different research tasks.
UAV mission planning and an autonomous art installation do not establish one narrow technology.
Reinforcement learning for UAV pursuit and estimation of low-altitude airspace capacity have different objects and outcomes.
Drone-racing visual attention and monocular autonomous landing solve different tasks.
Remote-ID separation and trajectory optimization for medical delivery are not one narrow planning method.
Collective UAV navigation and compartmentalization of binary mixtures have different research objects.
Inertial self-navigation and Kalman-filter object tracking are different estimation tasks.
Distributed convolution for airborne computing and federated-learning transmission scheduling are different computational methods.
Neuromorphic attitude control and EEG-based pilot-fatigue decoding have different technical aims.
Quadrotor trajectory planning and morphing-airframe aerodynamic design are different technical mechanisms.
Radio jamming detection and zero-knowledge authentication solve different security problems.
Titles share the IRS/RIS-assisted UAV communication family; the exact mechanism and article roles still require abstract and source review.
Photovoltaic-plant inspection and wilderness search are different applications and do not form one narrow line.
Human-pose benchmark and wildlife re-identification have different targets and research tasks.
Forest-canopy semantic SLAM and rooftop photogrammetric reconstruction are different mapping methods and settings.

limitations: Single-developer title-based rejection evidence, not independent expert annotation.
An explicit contrast can reject a narrow-line interpretation but absence of a contrast cannot confirm coherence.
No manual article-role classification, full-text review, independent-team verification, or signal Precision@15 is claimed.
